correctness.rationale: PASS: In real L4, Birkhoff–James orthogonality of unit x and y equals integral x³y=0. Put A=integral x²y², B=integral xy³. The exact quartic expansion is 1+lambda⁴+6A lambda²+4B lambda³, and Cauchy–Schwarz centered at A gives |B|<=sqrt[A(1-A²)]. The lower moment envelope D(A,lambda) is attained for every interior A by an explicit two-point distribution on any two positive finite-measure sets, with correct four moments and orthogonality. Fix lambda>0: strict concavity of sqrt[u(1-u²)] yields unique A minimizing D, parameterized by lambda(u)=3 sqrt[u(1-u²)]/(1-3u²), 0<u<1/sqrt3. An independent SymPy derivation checks the rational optimized G(u) and its exact derivative factor with quartic P(u)=9u⁴+9u³-12u²-3u+1; endpoint derivative and strict monotonicity give its unique root u*=0.200994344840... and sharp mu2=1.38784956695846... . Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz and uniqueness forces ratio y/x to take exactly the stated t± and L4 weights w±; no other maximizers. All conclusions require real L4 with at least two disjoint finite positive-measure sets, not complex L4 or mu1 or mu4.
